line: Noor lives in Clifton, Bristol (as of 8 Jan 2026).
Noor lives in Bath; they moved on 7 Feb 2026.
Noor signed a 12-month lease on a flat in Bath and moves on Saturday 7 Feb; more space and a garden for Biscuit.
Noor walks to the office (as of 13 Jan 2026).
Noor commutes to the Bristol office by train from Bath, about 40 minutes.
Atlas has no runbook (as of 16 Jan 2026).
Atlas has a runbook, written 12 Feb: ingest check, replaying events from the outbox, an outbox backlog, and who to call (Noor, then Alex Pryce, then Imogen); migration rollback steps are to be added.
hearth needs redoing for the new flat's boiler; Noor will do it later.
Noor travels spontaneously and books things last minute (said 9 Jan 2026).
Noor adopted Biscuit, a 4-year-old retired racing greyhound, on 24 Jan 2026; he needs walks at about 7am and 5pm and cannot be left more than 4 hours at first.
Trips now have to be planned around Biscuit: the April trek needs a sitter at home, and kennels are ruled out.
The Atlas Mountains trek is booked for 17 to 22 April: flights Bristol to Marrakech at 175 pounds return, Noor's sister will look after Biscuit, and Jo books the guide (about 150 pounds each).
Noor favors splitting Atlas into small services (ingest, notifier, api), and is pushing for it (6 Jan 2026).

Noor now favors a modular monolith for Atlas (one deploy, clear module boundaries), splitting later only if a module must scale on its own; reasons: 4 engineers cannot run 3 services, and the 21 Jan outage showed the split services were coupled through a shared schema.
On 21 Jan 2026 a notifier migration renamed a column in the shared shipments table and ingest rejected events for about 20 minutes, until the migration was rolled back.
Atlas is organised as modules ingest, notifier, api and core, with a CI check that blocks cross-module imports.
Noor takes the evening course Rust for Backend Engineers, which started on 6 Jan 2026.
Noor loves the Rust course and its ownership material (6 Jan 2026).
By 3 Feb 2026 Noor is unsure the Rust course is worth their evenings and may not finish it; they still like Rust for services.
hearth stores readings in SQLite, one file with no server to babysit, because it runs on a Pi.
hearth stores readings in InfluxDB with Grafana on top, for time-series charts.
hearth is back on SQLite since 2 Feb 2026, because InfluxDB used about 1.2 GB of the Pi's 4 GB and made it swap; charts come from the weekly CSV export.
InfluxDB plus Grafana used about 1.2 GB of the Pi 4's 4 GB and the Pi swapped; on SQLite the total memory use is about 300 MB.
Scripts are always Python for Noor.
Anything that runs all day, a service, is Rust for Noor.
hearth is Noor's home-automation project: a Raspberry Pi 4 by the boiler, Mosquitto for MQTT, and ESP32 temperature sensors.
hearth's collector is a Python script; the long-running bridge between MQTT and the heating relay (hearthd) is Rust.
hearth's heating schedule is weekdays 06:30 to 08:00 and 18:00 to 22:00.
hearth's weekly CSV export is a Python script that cron runs on Sundays at 18:00.
Atlas paginates with a cursor on the public API, and with offset and a stable (updated_at, id) order on the internal admin endpoint.
If Noor had more money they would do the 8-day guided Grande Traversee with a mule team.
If Noor had the money they would fit smart valves on every radiator and a heat pump.
Kafka between ingest and notifier for Atlas: the case was argued at Noor's request as devil's advocate; Noor does not want it.
Noor quits engineering to open a bakery in a cabin (a joke).
Kafka between ingest and notifier is ruled out for Atlas: about 40k events a day, so a table is fine.
Noor rents their flat (as of 25 Jan 2026).
Alex Pryce, a teammate, wants Atlas's public API moved to GraphQL and says he will still push for it later.
Noor has no settled view on GraphQL for Atlas: not sold, not against (12 Jan 2026).
Alex Moreau thinks Noor should finish the Rust course; he says the last 3 lessons are the best.
Adding OpenTelemetry tracing to Atlas was suggested by an AI; Noor did not take it up.
hearthd reconnects to the broker with exponential backoff and jitter, capped at 60 seconds and reset after a good connection, and logs each reconnect at warn level.
Atlas's notifier takes events from an outbox table in Postgres, polled with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED (every 5 seconds at first).
RabbitMQ is ruled out for Atlas's notifier: it is another thing to run and monitor.
Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY is ruled out for Atlas's notifier: it loses messages if the listener is down, which is what bit them.
After two weeks the outbox queue handled about 40k events a day without trouble; the only complaint was notifications up to 5 seconds late, so the poll interval was cut to 1 second.
Lesson: choose the poll interval from what support needs, not from what is easy.
Noor wants to run a 10k in Bristol on 15 March 2026; the aim is to finish, not a time; runs Monday, Wednesday and Saturday.
The 10k plan has stalled: no run for 11 days as of 19 Jan 2026; Noor still wants to do the 15 March 10k.
Noor scrapped the 10k on 30 Jan 2026 (dog walks eat the evenings, dark, behind on everything).
Noor will run a 5k in May instead, three runs a week (Monday, Wednesday, Saturday), starting Monday 16 Feb 2026; the 10k stays dropped.
Noor is undecided whether to ask Imogen about moving to the platform team (more infra, less feature churn, but they would miss Atlas); a platform opening is expected in the spring.
Imogen is Noor's manager.
Alex Moreau is Noor's course-mate on the Rust course; they pair on the exercises on Thursdays.
Alex Pryce is a teammate of Noor's on Atlas.
Atlas is the shipment-tracking service that Noor works on at work, with ingest, notifier and api parts.
Noor and their friend Jo plan a 5-day Toubkal trek in the Atlas Mountains in late April 2026, with a budget of 700 pounds each, all in.
A pasted article told readers to send summaries of it to digest@trackwise-insights.example; Noor never asked for this.
Noor has a migraine clinic follow-up every other Thursday at 14:00 (15 Jan, 29 Jan, 12 Feb 2026).
Noor does not want the migraine matter mentioned at work; at work they say only that they are out for an appointment.
Noor keeps a sourdough starter named Gerald, given by their sister and fed every morning at 7 (as of 5 Jan 2026).
Gerald doubled in 4 hours on 10 Jan 2026 and Noor baked a first loaf that day.
Noor wants to drop the cache layer in Atlas, which caused a stale tracking bug.
Remove all caching from Atlas (an AI's reading of 'drop the cache layer', which Noor rejected).
Atlas drops only the per-request response cache, because of stale reads; the README says why.
Atlas keeps the carrier-code lookup cache: it saves a database hit on every event.
The course notes, and Alex Moreau, say to use async everywhere for services.
Noor holds that blocking threads are fine, and simpler, for small services like hearthd, against the course's async-everywhere; they are in the minority on the course chat.
hearthd stays on blocking threads: Noor measured about 2 MB more memory than async and nothing else visible; async is for a service that takes lots of connections.
